process_observations.observation: Every name this step resolves by deploy-time lookup matched an artefact already on disk exactly: Tier_1_General as a queue file stem, and Email-Support / Email-Billing / Web as live CaseOrigin standard values.

The plan's build-scope declaration for this checker is load-bearing rather than decorative: a negative control changing webToCase/caseOrigin to WebPortal exits 1 naming the three legal values, which is an assertion that cannot exist at step scope.

No step in this build stamps a Case record type on an email or web case, so both channels land on the handling context's default - gotcha 9 instructs setting newEntityRecordType per routing address, and the string does not occur anywhere in plan.json.

Two per-address elements are named in email-to-case-configuration/references/well-architected.md line 39 with no description, example or second mention anywhere in the skill - fallbackQueue and routingFlow - and one of them would remove this build's dependence on the single shared defaultCaseOwner.

This file is the whole of Settings:Case for the build, and routingAddresses is a full-replacement list whose emailServicesAddress and isVerified cannot be restored once deleted, so deploying it as-is over an org that already has Email-to-Case configured would delete addresses it does not name.

useSystemEmailAddress is the one org-level lever in this file that reads on the sender axis D-M3S02-04 holds open, so it was omitted rather than set - which means the org's existing value stands until the M3 gate decides.

notifyDefaultCaseOwner true follows gotcha 8's explicit instruction to make the fallback loud, but Tier_1_General carries no queue email address and Q88 says Tier 1 takes no queue email, so the setting is either inert or contrary to Q88 and the guide does not say which.

standards/decision-trees/integration-pattern-selection.md has no branch for a native platform intake endpoint, so the direct-post Web-to-Case path this build recommends was grounded in the skill rather than routed by the declared tree.

Neither cited skill states whether CaseSettings child elements must follow the WSDL sequence, and a retrieved settings file is ordinarily alphabetical while the guide's sample definition is not, so this file's order is unverified until a validate-only run.
The step is built and untested; its declared build-scope checker, the always-on xml parse and the manifest check are the tester's to run and record.
